section: Follow one request through the system
purpose: Show the full service boundary, including unreleased routing and storage.
alt: DeepSeek Recipe converts JSON requests and responses to and from tokens. Entrypoints route to separate vision encoder, prefill and decode services, each with load balancing. Prefill and decode exchange KV state and connect to external KVCache Storage on 3FS. The complete storage and service orchestration are not all included in the release.
caption: Figure 2. The full system, not just the released engine. Reproduced unchanged from DeepSeek's deployment Q&A; Apache 2.0.

section: Preserve global history, rebuild a short local tail
purpose: Distinguish retained global context from approximate bounded local replay.
alt: The encoder prepares reusable global history over the prompt. The decoder reads that history but rebuilds its local sliding-window state from only a bounded suffix. Earlier prompt information is not discarded globally. The local replay boundary is approximate, and retained implementation tokens also cover speculative backtracking.
caption: Figure 3. Full global evidence, bounded local replay. Independent explanation of the released state boundary.

purpose: Explain overlap without implying impossible removal of sample dependencies or zero CPU work.
alt: A schematic compares serial scheduling, device execution and output processing with pipelined CPU and GPU work. In the overlap view, the CPU prepares another batch and handles older outputs while the device executes. Sample-dependent metadata is corrected before use. Bar lengths are not measurements.
caption: Figure 4. Hide avoidable gaps, not necessary dependencies. Schematic of the worker pipeline, not measured timings.

section: Prefill: throughput has a latency price
purpose: Preserve the source operating curve and its step-time versus throughput tradeoff.
alt: DeepSeek's prefill curve plots non-cached input tokens per second per GPU against milliseconds per prefill step. Context is 131072, EP4DP4 with 384 plus 32 experts and 140-token decoder replay. Larger per-rank token budgets raise throughput while increasing step time.
caption: Figure 5. More prefill work per step, more throughput and delay. Original DeepSeek release figure; Apache 2.0.

section: Decode: throughput and interactivity are different axes
purpose: Preserve the EP8/EP64 comparison with concurrency units and acceptance assumptions.
alt: Original decode comparison of EP64DP64 and EP8DP8 at context 131072, fixed nextn 3 and assumed per-token acceptance 75 percent. The horizontal axis is per-user token speed and the vertical axis is token throughput per GPU. Labels are requests per DP rank, not total cluster concurrency.
caption: Figure 6. Wider expert parallelism under one stated workload. Original DeepSeek comparison; both axes use the declared acceptance accounting.

purpose: Connect the request interface, four execution ideas and released-versus-surrounding-service boundary at a glance.
alt: Conceptual path: an API request passes through Recipe encoding, DeepInfer execution and Recipe streaming to an API response. The runtime targets DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM100 or Ascend 950. Four efficiency ideas are retained global history with short local replay, wide decode expert groups and busy-expert replicas, confidence-guided selection of a draft prefix for verification while skipping its suffix, and overlapping CPU bookkeeping with GPU work. Optimized attention, GEMM, expert communication and selected low precision support execution. The released offline engine and protocol libraries do not include complete production routing, persistent KV storage or service orchestration. Illustrative shapes and timelines are not measured performance.
caption: Figure 1. DeepInfer at a glance. AI-generated synthesis of the inspected release.
